title: Microsoft Teams: new SlimCore-based VDI optimisation for Omnissa Horizon on Mac endpoints
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap targets, licensing description and PowerShell controls are supported. It distinguishes the planned Omnissa Mac support from today's documentation, but should remove the unverified assertion that missing network rules specifically surface as failed screen sharing.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope: Users; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft plans SlimCore-based Teams VDI optimisation for Mac endpoints connecting to Omnissa Horizon.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams: New VDI solution for Omnissa on Mac; This feature allows Mac endpoints to optimize Microsoft Teams in VDI environments with the new SlimCore-based media engine

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The new optimisation runs the SlimCore media engine on the endpoint rather than the virtual machine.
claims.quote: SlimCore media engine (on the client) and msteams.exe (on the virtual desktop) now have a bidirectional channel and can start processing multimedia requests.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes an expanded feature set and improvements in quality, reliability and performance.
claims.quote: providing an expanded feature set and multiple improvements in quality, reliability and performance.

claims.claim: Learn currently lists Windows support for AVD/W365, Citrix, Omnissa and Amazon, and Mac support only for AVD/W365 and Citrix.
claims.quote: The new optimization supports Windows endpoints for AVD/W365, Citrix, Omnissa and Amazon. Mac is only supported on AVD/W365 and Citrix.

claims.claim: MsTeamsPluginOmnissa.dll is documented as bundled with Horizon Client for Windows 8.17 (2512) or higher.
claims.quote: For Omnissa Horizon, MsTeamsPluginOmnissa.dll is bundled with the Horizon Client for Windows 8.17 (2512) or higher.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The new optimisation is on by default for users who meet its minimum requirements.
claims.quote: Once you meet all the minimum requirements, launching Teams for the first time will attempt to load in SlimCore optimized mode, by default.

claims.claim: VDI2Optimization is Enabled by default at the Global org-wide level.
claims.quote: Enable Teams policy if necessary for a specific user group (it's enabled by default at a Global org-wide level). VDI2Optimization: Enabled (default value)

claims.claim: Teams attempts to load the new SlimCore optimisation when launched with the minimum requirements met.
claims.quote: Once you meet all the minimum requirements, launching Teams for the first time will attempt to load in SlimCore optimized mode, by default.

claims.claim: The new optimisation supports 1080p video, unlike WebRTC-based optimisation.
claims.quote: | 1080p | Yes | No |

claims.claim: The new optimisation supports Gallery View 3x3 and 7x7, unlike WebRTC-based optimisation.
claims.quote: | Gallery View 3x3 and 7x7 | Yes | No |

claims.claim: The new optimisation supports Quality of Service, unlike WebRTC-based optimisation.
claims.quote: | Quality of Service | Yes | No |

claims.claim: SlimCore makes media and signalling connections from the endpoint to peers or Teams servers.
claims.quote: MsTeamsVdi.exe is the process that makes all the TCP/UDP network connections to the Teams relays/conference servers or other peers (both signaling and media).

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: For Omnissa, outgoing screen sharing is sent from the virtual machine.
claims.quote: For Omnissa, Amazon or for MAC (Citrix or AVD/W365), the sharing is done directly between the user's virtual machine -the presenter- and the other peer -viewer- or conference server

claims.claim: Media flows as SRTP between the endpoint media engine and peers or Teams servers.
claims.quote: Then, Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP) media flows directly between MsTeamsVdi.exe and the other peer (or Teams Transport Relays or Conference servers).

claims.claim: The new Mac optimisation uses a downloaded media engine package running on the Mac.
claims.quote: the SlimCore package that is fetched and installed on macOS is the Framework only ('Microsoft.Teams.SlimCoreVdiBndl.mac').

claims.claim: For the documented Citrix and AVD Mac implementations, the plugin installs the media engine automatically and silently.
claims.quote: The Plugin is in charge of virtual channel establishment and automatic and silent media engine installation on the Mac device.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: How Horizon Client for Mac delivers its plugin and media engine is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams SlimCore Omnissa Horizon Mac minimum client plugin default licensing price meter; Teams Omnissa Horizon Mac SlimCore preview December 2026 default automatic rollout. Opened vdi-2 components, installation and Mac sections; only Windows Horizon delivery is documented.

claims.claim: The documented optimisation is initialised when Teams starts.
claims.quote: launching Teams for the first time will attempt to load in SlimCore optimized mode, by default.

claims.claim: SlimCore processes call media when users make or join calls or meetings.
claims.quote: Peer A selects the call button. MsTeamsVdi.exe communicates with the Microsoft Teams services in Azure, establishing an end-to-end signaling path with Peer B.

claims.claim: Omnissa virtual-machine screen sharing requires allowing Microsoft 365 network endpoint IDs 11 and 12 on the VM network.
claims.quote: therefore administrators must allow ID 11 and 12 on the VM's network as described in Microsoft 365 URLs and IP address ranges.

claims.claim: Missing network rules surface as failed screen sharing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams SlimCore Omnissa screen sharing fails virtual machine firewall ID 11 12. Opened vdi-2 networking and screen sharing, and vdi-2-troubleshooting. The VM network requirement is stated, but this specific failure symptom is not.
claims.fix: Remove 'Missing rules surface as failed screen sharing.' Keep the preceding documented requirement to allow IDs 11 and 12 on the virtual machine's network.

claims.claim: Horizon partner optimisation policies do not control the new mode; the Teams VDI policy does.
claims.quote: This policy now has an additional argument as the only configuration point to control whether or not a user can get the new optimization mode based on SlimCore. In other words, the VDI Partner's policy engines don't control the new optimization mode

claims.claim: A minimum Horizon Client for Mac version for SlimCore optimisation is not yet published.

claims.claim: Teams VDI policies are managed through the MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module.
claims.quote: Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsVdiPolicy -Identity <policy name> -VDI2Optimization Disabled updates a policy to disallow SlimCore optimisation.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsVdiPolicy -Identity RestrictedUserPolicy -VDI2Optimization "Disabled"; Disabled - disallow a user to be VDI 2.0 optimized.

claims.claim: No Teams admin center path for configuring VDI2Optimization is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams VDI policy VDI2Optimization DisableCallsAndMeetings Teams admin center user policy assignment UI; Teams admin center Teams VDI policy assign users VDI2Optimization DisableCallsAndMeetings UI. Opened vdi-2 and Set-CsTeamsVdiPolicy; results document PowerShell, not a VDI policy UI.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsVdiPolicy -Identity <user> -PolicyName <policy name> assigns a Teams VDI policy to a user.
claims.quote: Grant-CsTeamsVdiPolicy -identity "Ken Myer" -PolicyName RestrictedUserPolicy; In this example, a user with identity "Ken Myer" is being assigned the RestrictedUserPolicy

claims.claim: An admin UI for assigning Teams VDI policies is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams admin center Teams VDI policy assign users VDI2Optimization DisableCallsAndMeetings UI. Opened Grant-CsTeamsVdiPolicy and vdi-2. Search results describe calling/meeting policy UI separately, but give no VDI policy assignment UI.

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsVdiPolicy has a group assignment parameter set using -Group and -Rank.
claims.quote: GrantToGroup: Grant-CsTeamsVdiPolicy [[-PolicyName] <String>] [-Group] <String> -Rank <Int32>

claims.claim: Grant-CsTeamsVdiPolicy has a -Global parameter set for assigning a tenant-wide policy.
claims.quote: When you use this cmdlet without specifying a user identity, the policy applies to all users in your tenant. To skip a warning when you do this operation, specify "-Global".

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsVdiPolicy -Identity <policy name> -DisableCallsAndMeetings $true disables calls and joining meetings for non-optimised users.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsVdiPolicy [-DisableCallsAndMeetings <Boolean>] [-Identity] <String>; Set this to TRUE to disallow a non-optimized user to make calls, join meetings, and screen share from chat.

claims.claim: An admin UI for the Teams VDI DisableCallsAndMeetings setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams VDI policy VDI2Optimization DisableCallsAndMeetings Teams admin center user policy assignment UI; Teams admin center Teams VDI policy assign users VDI2Optimization DisableCallsAndMeetings UI. Opened Set-CsTeamsVdiPolicy and vdi-2; no UI for this VDI-specific setting was found.

claims.claim: DisableCallsAndMeetings applies to non-optimised VDI users, including users whose new optimisation fails to load.
claims.quote: Determines whether a user on a non-optimized Vdi environment can make all types of calls. Set this to FALSE to allow a non-optimized user to make calls, join meetings, and screen share from chat.

claims.quote: This policy now has an additional argument as the only configuration point to control whether or not a user can get the new optimization mode based on SlimCore.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout

claims.quote: New-CsTeamsVdiPolicy -Identity RestrictedUserPolicy -VDI2Optimization "Disabled"; The command shown here uses the New-CsTeamsVdiPolicy cmdlet to create a new VDI policy

claims.claim: The Teams VDI Status Indicator identifies the new optimisation.
claims.quote: It also shows if they're using the WebRTC optimization or the new Slimcore-based one by hovering their cursor over the Optimized banner.

claims.claim: The troubleshooting page lists connection error codes for the new optimisation.
claims.quote: Error Codes 2000 ("No Plugin") and 2003 ("Virtual Channel not allowed") are the most likely causes.

claims.claim: A pilot Teams VDI policy assignment can be removed.
claims.quote: To remove a specific assignment and fall back to the default tenant policy, you can assign to $Null.
